facts.text: The resort has a clifftop setting in Seogwipo City on Jeju Island.
facts.excerpt: From a clifftop setting in Seogwipo City

facts.text: It was the first JW Marriott Resort and Spa in South Korea.
facts.excerpt: This first JW Marriott Resort and Spa in South Korea was designed by award‑winning interior designer Bill Bensley.

facts.text: The interiors were designed by Bill Bensley, inspired by Jeju's canola fields and basalt walls.
facts.excerpt: Renowned designer Bill Bensley drew inspiration from the local vibrant canola fields and iconic basalt walls to create JW Marriott Jeju's luxurious interiors.

facts.text: Bensley chose yellow as the main color for its symbolic representation of luck in Korean culture, with gray, black and white echoing Jeju's volcanic terrain.
facts.excerpt: Bensley chose yellow as the main color for its symbolic representation of luck in Korean culture. Secondary colors of gray, black, and white echo Jeju's volcanic terrain.

facts.text: Architecture firm WATG drew inspiration from Korea's indigenous Choga architecture and Jeju's terrain, with modern reinterpretations of Choga-style roofs.
facts.excerpt: Renowned architectural firm, WATG, drew inspiration from Korea's indigenous Choga architecture and Jeju's unique terrain to craft our internationally acclaimed resort.

facts.text: The JW Garden sits alongside the Jeju Olle Trail route 7, with views of the sea.
facts.excerpt: nestled alongside the Jeju Olle Trail route 7, offering picturesque views of the beautiful sea of Jeju

facts.text: Most rooms include a balcony with ocean views.
facts.excerpt: Most rooms at our Jeju Island family resort include a balcony with ocean views.

facts.text: The Panorama Suite is designed to offer ocean views from every angle.
facts.excerpt: Panorama Suite, uniquely designed to offer breathtaking ocean views from every angle

facts.text: The Family Suite has a king bedroom, a second bedroom with two twin bunk beds for children, and a separate living room.
facts.excerpt: Bedroom 1 boasts a lavish King-sized bed, Bedroom 2 is adorned with 2 twin bunk beds for children, and the additional allure of a separate living room

facts.text: Rooms have marble bathtubs.
facts.excerpt: Recharge in hotel lodging with LED TVs, minibars, marble bathtubs, and free WiFi.

facts.text: The outdoor pool is a heated infinity pool with a swim-up bar.
facts.excerpt:
Swim-up Bar

Infinity Pool

facts.text: SPA by JW offers Hot Stone, Deep Tissue and Swedish treatments in five treatment rooms.
facts.excerpt: skilled therapists offer personalized Hot Stone, Deep Tissue, and Swedish treatments in five tranquil rooms

facts.text: The resort has a jimjilbang, a Korean-style sauna with various themed rooms.
facts.excerpt: a jimjilbang (Korean-style sauna) with various themed rooms

facts.text: The Re Play Kids Club offers half-day and full-day Kids Camp programs with activities and cooking sessions.
facts.excerpt: Allow the kids to enjoy fun activities and cooking sessions, with flexible half-day and full-day programs lasting up to 8 hours.

facts.text: The resort's 'RE CONNECT' activity program is curated for families, couples, solo guests and children.
facts.excerpt: With the theme "RE CONNECT," we have thoughtfully curated activities for families, couples, solo guests, and children!

facts.text: Soombi-Sori is a meditation and breathing experience inspired by Jeju's haenyeo, the island's female divers.
facts.excerpt: A meditation and breathing experience inspired by the lives and breath of Jeju’s female divers.

facts.text: Art Climbing is a journey through artworks across the resort.
facts.excerpt: Journey through artworks across the resort and discover the narratives of Jeju’s nature, culture, and way of life from a new perspective.

facts.text: The Flying Hog is a wood-fire grill showcasing Jeju's seasonal ingredients.
facts.excerpt: The Flying Hog is a signature wood-fire grill showcasing the island's finest seasonal ingredients

facts.text: Yeoumul offers a chef-led journey inspired by Jeju's haenyeo culture.
facts.excerpt: a chef-led journey inspired by Jeju’s haenyeo culture at Yeoumul

facts.text: The Lounge is a tea lounge by day and a Korean-style jumak by night.
facts.excerpt: The Lounge transforms from a relaxed tea lounge by day into a Korean-style jumak by night

facts.text: Dishes use fresh vegetables and herbs from the JW Garden.
facts.excerpt: using local ingredients, including fresh vegetables and herbs from JW Garden

facts.text: The resort received One MICHELIN Key in the inaugural MICHELIN Key Hotels Selection.
facts.excerpt: JW Marriott Jeju Resort & Spa has been awarded One MICHELIN Key, part of the inaugural MICHELIN Key Hotels Selection

facts.text: Jeju International Airport is about 40 km from the hotel.
facts.excerpt: CJU is located approximately 40.0 KM from the hotel.

facts.text: Pets are not allowed.
facts.excerpt: No, pets are not allowed at JW Marriott Jeju Resort & Spa.

facts.text: On-site self parking is complimentary for guests.
facts.excerpt: Self parking is complimentary for guests.

facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler describes the resort as a sprawling, straight-lined complex of basalt rock on a cliff on the island's southern tip.
facts.excerpt: Pitched up on a cliff on the island’s southern tip, the JW Marriott Jeju Resort & Spa is a sprawling, straight-lined complex of basalt rock.

facts.text: The lobby has frames of timber hanok, traditional Korean buildings, that mimic the island's oldest settlements.
facts.excerpt: the frames of timber hanok (traditional Korean buildings) in the lobby mimic the island’s oldest settlements
